description: The hand-verified expected result for the positive Gitleaks fixture. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/gitleaks.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match.
scanner_class_note: Fixed per tool by AAP 0.5.4's class table and authored as a constant in the adapter (SCANNER_CLASS). Trivy is the single tool whose class varies per record; this one never does, so no row below takes its class from record content.
rules: No user-specified rule governs this file. review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided.', which is the whole document; AAP 0.7 says the same. No rule is cited or invented here, and the absence is not licence to lower the bar -- the bar on this file is a security property, stated under redaction_invariant and asserted against this file's own bytes.

fixture.provenance_note: The raw artifact holds exactly one record -- this provisioning's single leak -- and element 0 is that record field for field, key order included, unmodified. The remaining five carry the same eighteen keys in the same order and name real files at real lines in the pinned tree, so they reach what one record cannot: a Scala main source, a Python test module inside python/pyspark/**, a Dockerfile under the Kubernetes docker root, a five-line manifest, and a lockfile outside the twelve globs. Each element's provenance -- captured or derived -- is stated per row under row_derivations.source rather than left for a reader to assume.
fixture.captured_element_equality: Element 0 was compared to the raw artifact's sole record key by key and found equal, including key order. That equality is asserted here, not assumed, and the recorded sha256 above is what makes a later edit to the fixture visible: these rows are re-derived when it changes rather than patched to agree.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations, and the one row matching none of them is named there too.

reference_behaviours.what_this_file_fixes: severity_native null and severity_norm Info on every row, with the basis 'no_vocabulary' stated rather than an Info level silently assumed.
reference_behaviours.why_it_belongs_here: The fixture carries no Severity key anywhere -- Gitleaks defines no severity vocabulary at all -- so this is the folder's reference assertion for that path. A test that checked only the two field values would pass equally against an adapter that hard-coded Info, which is why the basis is stated as an expected value beside them.

reference_behaviours.what_this_file_fixes: Every path below is the record's File taken against the base recorded for this runner, whose kind is scan_root, so the value is root-relative and unchanged.
reference_behaviours.why_it_belongs_here: A wrong base mis-resolves every Gitleaks row while every value still looks plausible: nothing about a path like a Scala source under core/src/main reveals which directory it was relative to. The base is therefore read from runner-metadata.json rather than inferred from the paths themselves.

resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, tools.gitleaks.path_base -- read as input, never assumed. Its record_path_field is 'File'.
resolution_context.path_base_value_note: The recorded base is the pinned scan root. Its absolute form is deliberately not reproduced here: no absolute path appears anywhere in this file, and these rows hold for whatever absolute root the adapter is given.
resolution_context.recorded_invocation_shape: Eighteen invocations, each handed exactly one root-relative directory, with the runner's working directory set to the scan root.
resolution_context.invocation_source: runner-metadata.json tools.gitleaks.invocation_form and working_directory, corroborated independently by harness/bin/run-gitleaks.sh (it cds to the scan root, then loops one directory per invocation) and by harness/ENVIRONMENT.md's path-base table.
resolution_context.why_the_base_is_invocation_dependent: gitleaks dir takes exactly one path and reports relative to the process working directory when handed more, so the base is a property of the invocation rather than of the tool (AAP 0.5.4). Both shapes are real: the historical harness AAP 0.2.3 describes passed all eighteen scope directories to a single invocation, and this provisioning passes one per invocation.
resolution_context.invariance_across_the_two_shapes: Here the two shapes give the same base, because the runner's working directory is the scan root: one root-relative directory per invocation reports File relative to that root, and eighteen paths in one invocation would report relative to the working directory, which is that same root. Every path below therefore holds under either reading. That is a fact about this provisioning, not a licence to skip reading the metadata -- a runner that cds elsewhere would need these paths re-derived, and no runner may be edited to make one shape true (AAP 0.3.2).
resolution_context.path_basis_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, BASIS_ALREADY_ROOT_RELATIVE -- the basis resolve_recorded_path records where the recorded base and the scan root are the same location, so the reported File was already root-relative and the join changed nothing. The basis says so rather than implying a resolution that did no work.
resolution_context.path_kind_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, path_kind_for: no '!' separator and no leading '..' segment, so every path names a location inside the scanned tree. Whether the file exists on disk is a separate question, and each of the six does exist at the pin -- recorded per row.
resolution_context.severity_source: None. The eighteen keys a pinned-Gitleaks record carries include no severity-like field, and the fixture carries no Severity key anywhere, so every row goes through severity.SeverityResult.absent().
resolution_context.severity_basis_authority: harness/lib/normalize/severity.py, BASIS_NO_VOCABULARY. absent() carries severity_native null, severity_norm Info and that basis, and its __post_init__ refuses a severity_native on it -- so the absence is structural rather than a convention a caller has to remember.
resolution_context.severity_selected_entry_note: null on this path: nothing was used to derive the band, so there is neither a label nor a score entry to record. The band comes from a policy fixed before any output was observed, and no native literal is synthesised -- inventing one would put a literal into oss-scan-results/severity-map.md that the tool never emitted.
resolution_context.severity_map_consequence: The tally is fed once per emitted row, which is what lets severity-map.md name gitleaks as a tool that defines no severity vocabulary and put a row count behind the statement rather than only an assertion.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A secret finding names a code location rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry. AAP 0.5.4's unformable-coordinate rejection reaches dependency-oriented records only, so the absence here is not a rejection condition.
resolution_context.cwe_and_cve: null on every row. The shape carries no weakness or advisory identifier; deriving a CWE from a rule id would be inference of exactly the kind AAP 0.5.4 forbids.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of the top-level array -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction; its _count_gitleaks is the array's length and nothing else
counts.every_element_yields_exactly_one_outcome: One row or one rejection per element, never both and never neither. All six become rows: each carries a non-empty RuleID and Description, a non-empty root-relative File, and a StartLine that is an integer of at least 1, so no rejection condition is met.
counts.row_order: fixture order, preserved. Both output files use it and emit.py compares them ordered row by row, so an expected file in any other order would assert something the pipeline does not promise.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/gitleaks.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): six authored keys, then one path_kind_* per normalize.paths.PATH_KINDS member and one severity_basis_* per normalize.severity.BASIS_VALUES member -- fifteen keys in that order, which is the key set and the order above. Deliberately absent from it, and so from here: any adapter-side count of records walked, rows or rejections. Those are len(rows), len(rejections) and reconcile.count_records, and a plausible substitute published here is how the independent-traversal requirement would quietly be lost.
counters_note: severity_absent is 6 and severity_basis_no_vocabulary is 6 by policy rather than by observation: every row of this tool takes that path, so the counters state the number instead of asserting the rule. rows_in_scope plus rows_out_of_scope is 5 + 1 = 6, one measurement split rather than a second count of the same thing.

counters_aap_0_5_4_reported.note: The four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool. Two of them -- multi_location_records and non_filesystem_paths -- are keys of this adapter's own counter set and appear above with the same values. The other two are not: a Gitleaks record carries no CWE or CVE field at all, so no record can be multi-valued in either, and the adapter keys no counter it could never increment. They are stated here as 0 by construction so the four required numbers are all present in one place, and so that the difference between 'measured 0' and '0 because the field does not exist in this shape' is legible rather than inferred from a missing key.

redaction_invariant.requirement: AAP 0.5.4: Gitleaks runs with redaction so a matched secret's value never enters an artifact, and no adapter carries a secret value into any field. This file is committed to git -- .gitignore line 31 matches artifacts/ and nothing under oss-scan-results/ -- so the invariant has to hold of this file as written, not only of the dataset the adapter produces.
redaction_invariant.message_source_on_every_row: Description, the rule's own description. Never Secret, never Match, and never Message, which is a git commit message rather than a description. There is deliberately no fallback: every candidate would either infer content the tool did not state or carry a captured value into the field.
redaction_invariant.keys_never_read_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/gitleaks.py, NEVER_READ_FIELDS. Fingerprint is excluded even though this artifact's value is a file-rule-line composite: in commit mode it also carries a commit identity, and a field whose safety depends on which mode ran is not a field to read.
redaction_invariant.keys_read_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/gitleaks.py, SOURCE_FIELDS -- the four keys a row is built from, named one at a time. The record is never copied, spread or iterated into a row, which is what makes the invariant structural there; here it is upheld by deriving each of the twelve values from those four keys and fixed constants alone.
redaction_invariant.symlink_file_is_the_one_exception: SymlinkFile is the single key outside SOURCE_FIELDS the adapter looks at, and only through a predicate returning a bool. It is a filesystem path rather than a captured value, it is never emitted, and it is never substituted for an absent File. It is empty on all six elements here, so it decides nothing beyond leaving multi_location_records at 0.
redaction_invariant.check_performed: Every distinct Match, Secret and Fingerprint value in the fixture -- eight values across the six elements -- was tested as a substring against the whole of this file. Zero hits, which is the required result. The check covers prose as well as row fields, and two drafting consequences follow from it: no sentence here quotes the placeholder string the runner's redaction flag substitutes for a captured value, and nowhere is a path, a rule id and a line number joined into one colon-separated string, since that is the shape of this artifact's fingerprint values.
redaction_invariant.upstream_protection_is_not_the_check: The runner passes a redaction flag, so a captured value never reached the artifact in the first place. That is upstream protection in a runner this run may not edit, and it is not a substitute for the assertion above, which is made against this file's own bytes.

prohibitions_observed.no_cross_tool_interpretation: Trivy's adapter also reports secrets. A location both tools report is two rows in two expected files with no comment: nothing here compares tools, ranks them, explains why one found something another did not, or folds one into the other (AAP 0.3.2).
prohibitions_observed.no_judging: No row is characterised as real, important, a false positive or a duplicate, and no row's rule or location is glossed as the sort of thing that tends to be one. Whether anything named below is worth acting on is not this dataset's question -- the row records what the tool reported, at the location the tool reported it, and stops.
prohibitions_observed.no_dedup: Three elements share a RuleID and a Description; they are three records and three rows. Two byte-identical elements would likewise be two rows.
prohibitions_observed.no_invented_severity: The tool defines no severity vocabulary, so none is invented: severity_native stays null and severity_norm comes from the fixed no-vocabulary policy rather than from a guess at what a finding deserves.
prohibitions_observed.kept_not_filtered: The out-of-glob lockfile row is kept with in_scope false and counted, never dropped (AAP 0.9.3). Only evidence about the runner establishes a wrong scan root (AAP 0.8.3), and the recorded metadata shows this runner resolved the pinned root.
prohibitions_observed.never_derived_by_running_the_adapter: Every value in this file was read out of the fixture and the authored contracts. Nothing here was produced by invoking the adapter and recording its output, which would make the test a tautology: the adapter would be asserted to agree with itself.
prohibitions_observed.agreement_check_disclosed: After these values were derived and written, the adapter was invoked over this fixture once and its rows, rejections and counters compared to what is recorded here; agreement was complete. That is disclosed in the same spirit as the corroboration below: it followed derivation, it could only ever have surfaced a disagreement to diagnose, and it contributed no value to this file. A reader who wants the derivation checked should check it against the fixture and the contracts, which is what every row_derivations entry below is for.

corroboration.note: The committed dataset carries exactly one gitleaks row -- the captured record row 0 is derived from -- and all twelve fields agree, including severity_native null, severity_norm Info, start_line 3090 and in_scope true; the CSV's severity_native cell is empty, which is that same absence under the CSV convention. Corroboration recorded after the fact, not the source of these values, so a future disagreement between this file and the adapter is a finding to diagnose rather than a diff to apply.
corroboration.derived_elements_have_no_counterpart: The five derived elements appear in no dataset row by construction, so nothing corroborates them and nothing needs to: each was hand-derived from the fixture against the authored contracts, and their expected values are checkable by reading those two things.

row_derivations.out_of_scope_reason: The path matches none of the twelve globs -- dev/ is not among the scope roots -- so in_scope is false. It is not a rejection, not a filter and not a judgement about the finding; the row is emitted and counted under rows_out_of_scope.

in_scope_verification.method: Each path was matched against the twelve globs by hand and then checked twice more, with two implementations that are not the one under test: a glob-to-regex translation written for this check, and CPython 3.13's PurePosixPath.full_match, whose ** spans zero or more directories. All three agree on all six paths.
in_scope_verification.why_not_fnmatch: Three of the twelve globs depend on ** matching zero or more directories, and neither fnmatch nor PurePath.match provides those semantics. A matcher built on either silently drops whole modules, and a silently dropped module looks exactly like a module with nothing to report (AAP 0.5.4).
in_scope_verification.src_test_rule: The exclusion is the literal substring src/test. No path here contains it, including the Python test module, whose test-ness is expressed as a tests/ directory and a test_ filename rather than a Maven src/test tree.
in_scope_verification.result: five in scope, one out of scope and kept
